narrative.overview:
The page is a railway signal-box mimic panel, not a website wearing a theme. A pale enamel board with a printed 24px mosaic grid carries black track strips; each of the eleven projects is a numbered route drawn left to right from what goes in to what comes out, with station plates along the track. Setting a route lights it: a white centre line appears in steps, the station borders light one after another, and a red occupancy block runs the length of the track. The panel is the argument - the whole network is visible at once, so a recruiter can read eleven projects in one glance instead of scrolling a stack of cards.

Everything is either printed on enamel or mounted on it. Printed things are Archivo, black on green-grey, with no container except the page itself. Mounted things are black traffolyte plates with engraved ivory caps in B612 Mono: the name bar, section headings, station labels, buttons, the route numbers, the legend. One control is illuminated - the yellow Email push button - and it is the only warm colour on the board. The result is calm, instrument-like and slightly industrial: dense with information, quiet in colour, and legible at a glance because the structure (IN to stations to OUT) repeats eleven times.

Motion is the panel doing its job, never decoration. Light arrives in discrete steps rather than fades, because a lamp is either lit or not. Nothing floats, glows neon, scans, or loops as a gimmick; the one sustained movement is the auto-route cycle, and it can be stopped.
keyCharacteristics: Enamel board + 24px printed tile grid as the page, never a dark background.
Black track strips, white route lamps, one red occupancy block: the schematic is the layout.
Two typefaces only: Archivo (voice) and B612 Mono (labels, numbers, plates).
Round route-number badges as the only repeated circle besides lamps.
One yellow push button per viewport, for Email.
Stepped, relay-like motion; a complete still panel under reduced motion.

rules.name: The Two Lamps Rule
rules.body: Green means available, red means occupied/running. No third status colour, no colour-coded technology logos, no red for emphasis.

rules.name: The Yellow Belongs to Email Rule
rules.body: The yellow appears on the primary action and nowhere else; one yellow element per viewport, and it always says Email.

rules.name: The Enamel Is the Page Rule
rules.body: Black is equipment mounted on enamel, never the page behind it. A full-bleed dark section breaks the world.

rules.name: The Plate Speaks Mono Rule
rules.body: Anything mounted on black is B612 Mono in caps. Anything printed on enamel is Archivo. A sentence in mono on enamel or a sans-serif label on a plate is the tell that the world has slipped.

rules.name: The Expanded Name Rule
rules.body: The width axis is used for hierarchy, not decoration: 125% on the name and section plates, 118% on case titles, 112% on card titles and the push button, 100% for all body text.

rules.name: The Left-to-Right Rule
rules.body: Every route reads IN on the left and OUT on the right, and every station is lit in that order. Nothing on the panel flows right-to-left, and the vertical mobile diagrams keep the same top-to-bottom order.

rules.name: The One Panel Rule
rules.body: The eleven projects live inside one keylined panel. Adding a twelfth means a twelfth row, never a second panel or a card grid beside it.

rules.name: The Thickness Rule
rules.body: A hard offset is material, not decoration: same-hue darker, 5px or less, on a control that physically depresses. Offset shadows in ink or accent hues under text, cards or headings are not part of this world.

dos: Do draw every project as a route with named IN and OUT terminals, numbered in the same order as the panel (01-11).
Do keep the 24px enamel grid visible behind all content; it is the board, not a texture on cards.
Do mount labels, numbers, dates and status on black plates with mono caps; use 3px corners at this size.
Do light routes in steps (150ms stagger, steps() easing) and let the red block be the only thing that travels.
Do put every screenshot inside a black VDU bezel at 10px radius with a lamp-dot caption naming the live demo.
Do keep body text on enamel at 17px/1.55 with 36-62ch measures; the panel is dense, not cramped.
donts: Don't put a kicker or eyebrow line above a heading; the plate heading is the label and the name is the headline.
Don't add a dark full-bleed section, neon glow, scanlines, CRT curvature, or a terminal window chrome - the world is an enamel panel, not an IDE.
Don't round a rectangle past 10px, or use pills for anything but the Email push and the auto switch.
Don't colour-code technologies, add gradients, glass, or a fourth signal colour beyond green/red/yellow.
Don't animate lamp light with a smooth fade, bounce, or infinite attention loop; only the auto-route cycle repeats, and it must be stoppable.
Don't place a sans-serif label on a plate or a mono paragraph on enamel; the material decides the typeface.
Don't invent metrics, hero copy or a second yellow element to fill space; empty enamel is on-world.
